questions.q: According to Byron Katie, what actually causes a person’s stress?
a: Their interpretation of events, not the events themselves
Other people’s behavior and unavoidable external events
A chemical imbalance that requires professional treatment
The lack of a clear plan for controlling the future
questions.why: Lesson 1 says stress comes from how we process events; change the interpretation and the stress changes.

questions.q: What is the first of the four questions in “The Work”?
a: Is this thought true?
How should I fix this problem?
What would a friend tell me to do?
Why does this always happen to me?
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the questions in order, beginning with whether the stressful thought is true.

a: Flipping a thought into several versions and noticing how each feels
Replacing every negative thought with an equally positive one
Repeating a thought until your feelings about it disappear
Asking someone else to judge whether the thought is fair
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes turning the original thought around in various ways and observing your reaction to each.

questions.q: What does the summary say about complaining about things you cannot control?
a: It changes nothing and has no value, so it is wasted energy
It relieves tension and helps you move on faster
It shows others that you care about doing things well
It is useful when the person responsible can hear you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says complaining has a value of zero and you cannot change reality by being frustrated about it.

questions.q: What should you do about realities that are outside your control?
a: Find your place within them and do what you can
Keep resisting them until they finally change
Ignore them completely and focus only on your goals
Wait for better circumstances before taking any action
questions.why: Lesson 3 advises accepting what you cannot control and acting where you can, which is what brings happiness.
